name: Build cover
summary: The unit puts up pieces of cover or obstacles that stay on the map until destroyed: sandbag lines that stop bullets for whoever crouches behind them, wire that stops or slows soldiers, tank traps that stop vehicles, or walls that block both. Each piece is placed as an outline and built up over a few seconds, cheaply, while the builder is exposed. The pieces shape where fights happen: they make cover where the map has none, close gaps and funnel the enemy into a kill zone. Explosives, shelling and heavy vehicles break them, and enemies can use sandbags too.
counterplay: Blow it up: grenades, rockets, mortars, artillery and tank shells break sandbags and walls that shrug off rifle fire (Company of Heroes, Battlefield V).
Drive through it: medium and heavy vehicles crush wire and sandbags, and only heavy tanks crush tank traps (Company of Heroes; mechs flatten Iron Harvest sandbags and wire).
Cut or take it down: engineers cut wire or dismantle it with a wrench (Company of Heroes, Foxhole), and Supreme Commander engineers reclaim walls almost at once.
Go around: a line has ends and gaps; infantry walks between tank traps, vehicles roll over wire, and aircraft ignore all of it.
Use it yourself: sandbags give cover to anyone behind them, so take the enemy's line from the open side or flank it (Company of Heroes).
Hit the builder: building takes time in the open, so shoot the engineer before the line is up, and shell positions while their cover is still thin.

other_examples.unit: Sand Bags, Barbed Wire and Tank Traps (Engineers, Pioneers, Sappers and some line infantry)
other_examples.note: Builder squads lay free obstacles as lines dragged from one end to the other, a few seconds per piece. Sandbags give heavy cover to any soldier behind them, friend or foe, and block infantry and light vehicles; wire gives no cover but stops infantry and is used to funnel them into machine-gun fire; tank traps stop vehicles of both sides while soldiers walk through, so players put wire behind them. Explosives, mortars and tank fire break sandbags, medium and heavy vehicles crush sandbags and wire, heavy tanks crush tank traps, and some engineers cut wire.

sources.title: Sand Bags, Company of Heroes Wiki
Barbed Wire, Company of Heroes Wiki
Tank Traps, Company of Heroes Wiki

other_examples.note: Cheap tech 1 wall segments with a lot of health, used to funnel attackers into point defences and artillery and to keep short-range units away from long-range ones. They are too low to stop most fire. Units don't shoot walls unless ordered to, one segment at a time, so the quickest way through is an engineer reclaiming them.

The Sentry spends energy on a short-lived barrier that ground units can't pass; massive units break it, and aircraft ignore it. Players use it to seal a ramp against a rush, cut off reinforcements or a retreat, split the enemy army, or stop enemies from kiting their melee units.

sources.title: Force Field, Liquipedia StarCraft II Wiki

other_examples.note: Beside capturing buildings, the Soviet combat engineer can pay for a bunker on a long cooldown, which friendly infantry then garrison and fire from.

sources.title: Combat engineer (Red Alert 3), Command & Conquer Wiki

other_examples.unit: Guard Tower (deployed by the GDF Engineer)
other_examples.note: The Engineer has a tower brought to a target spot; up to four infantry units garrison it and fire out of it, enemy engineers can capture it, and in multiplayer it can heal nearby allied infantry for a short time.

shooter_analogues.unit: Sandbag Cover, Sandbag Wall and Barbed Wire (player-built field fortifications)
shooter_analogues.note: A player opens the build menu, lays a curved blueprint between two ends and carries the materials into it. Sandbag cover protects crouching soldiers and can be vaulted; upgraded to a wall it is tall enough to stand behind. Barbed wire slows infantry of both sides but not vehicles, shrugs off almost all damage and is removed with a wrench or an explosive. Unmaintained works decay over time, trucks ram sandbags, and build sites are fragile until finished.

Every class carries a build tool and can raise walls, sandbags, wire and tank obstacles, but only at fixed spots on the map shown as outlines to players holding the tool; Support builds twice as fast and several builders together go faster. Fortifications belong to no side, resist small arms and fall only to explosives and vehicles, and the builder earns an assist when a teammate scores a kill while resting a bipod on them.

On a cooldown, Mei raises a row of ice pillars at a spot in front of her that blocks sight, movement and attacks for a few seconds; every pillar can be broken separately, she can turn the wall lengthwise or across before casting, and she can shatter it early.

Rampart holds a few charges of a crouch-height wall with an upper barrier that takes a short moment to finish. The barrier stops enemy shots from the front while her team's shots fired out through it hit harder; the base and the barrier have separate health, and losing the base removes the whole wall.

Players spend gathered wood, stone or metal to snap walls, floors, ramps and roofs onto a grid in the middle of a fight; wood goes up fastest but is weakest, metal the reverse. Pieces must connect to the ground or they collapse, anyone's weapons can break them, and a placement preview shows whether a spot is free. The mode without building proved popular enough to become its own playlist.

player_translation.summary: A builder (an engineer, a pioneer walker, a support drone) carries a small stock of cover pieces and lays them where its team needs to hold or where the enemy must not pass. Each piece is placed as a ghost outline, built over a couple of seconds while the builder is exposed, and then stays until destroyed or until the builder leaves the match. Cover is shared terrain, not a buff: anyone can hide behind sandbags, so the skill is placing it so that only your side benefits.
as_user: You carry a few cover pieces, shown as pips. Press Q to show a ghost of the current piece at your aim point, drag to set its length and direction (like Company of Heroes and Foxhole lines between two points), and click to start building; hold the key, or keep your tool on it, until it is up.

You pick the piece from a small radial menu: sandbags that stop bullets for soldiers crouching behind them, wire that stops or slows infantry, or tank traps that stop vehicles. Your variant may add a bunker your teammates can enter.

Building takes a few seconds per piece and you can't shoot while you build, so you build before the fight or behind a teammate's guns. Teammates with a build tool can help, and several builders finish it faster.
Your pieces refill at a resupply point or from a teammate's supply kit. A cap keeps only so many of your pieces on the map; building past it removes your oldest.
You get assist points when a teammate kills an enemy while using your cover, as Battlefield V rewards its builders.
as_target: You see the pieces plainly: a sandbag line, a coil of wire, steel hedgehogs, each with a team-coloured trim that tells you who built it.
Right now you can go around the end of the line, blow a gap with a grenade or rocket, drive a heavy vehicle through wire and sandbags, cut wire with a repair tool, or call artillery on the position.
Sandbags are cover for you too: reach the open side and the enemy's line protects you.
Shoot the builder while the outline is still going up: half-built pieces are weak and don't stop bullets yet.
teammates: The builder's team holds the line: riflemen and machine-gunners take the cover, a turret or a minefield covers the gap the wire leaves open, and resupply players refill the builder's stock.
Several builders raise a position fast, and a squad can agree where the line goes before the enemy arrives.
The enemy team brings splash and heavy vehicles to break the line, engineers to cut wire, and flankers to take the cover from behind.
Bait and trap: wire funnels attackers into the one open gap, where the defenders' guns or mines wait (Company of Heroes kill zones).
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse fires the unit's weapon.

Q: hold to show the ghost piece at the aim point (within a short reach); drag to set length and angle; release to place the outline. Then hold Q (or the repair tool's fire) next to it to build; letting go pauses the build.
Mouse wheel while holding Q cycles the piece (sandbags, wire, tank traps, bunker) on a card that has more than one; a card with one piece skips the menu.
Removing your own piece: hold the interact key on it to take it down and get the piece back.
The pattern spends one counted key (Q); helping a teammate build and cutting enemy wire use the shared interact key and the repair tool.
feedback: Placement: a ghost outline, green where it fits and red where it doesn't (as in Foxhole and Fortnite), with a small arrow showing which side is the protected side.
Building: hammering sounds and pieces stacking up, a progress ring, and a piece that turns solid when finished.
Protection: a soldier behind finished sandbags shows a small shield icon, so both teams know who has cover.
Damage: pieces visibly crumble as they lose health and break into rubble that stays for a moment, so a fresh gap is easy to spot from above.
Wire and tank traps get bold silhouettes and a team-coloured trim, readable at a glance from a top-down camera.
changes_from_rts: RTS builders lay long lines for free or nearly free (Company of Heroes) and an AI squad takes the cover. Here pieces come from a small stock with a cap, so one player can't wall off a map, and the player has to take the cover themselves.
RTS cover gives a hidden bonus to accuracy and suppression. In a shooter cover must physically stop bullets and block movement, with a visible protected side, or players won't trust it.

Supreme Commander walls are ignored by units until ordered, and Foxhole works decay over hours; here cover simply has health, every weapon can damage it, and it is removed when its builder leaves, so the map doesn't clog with old walls.
A builder in an RTS is a cheap unit in the back; here the builder is a player who wants to fight, so building is fast (seconds per piece) and helping teammates speeds it up.
Iron Harvest lets engineers fortify any open ground; here no-build areas around spawns, objectives' centres and doors stop players from sealing them shut.

team_play.notes: Cover changes the map for both teams: the builder decides where fights happen, defenders take the cover and guard the gaps, and support players refill the stock. Attackers answer with splash, heavy vehicles, wire-cutting engineers and flankers, and anyone can steal a sandbag line from its open side.

notes: Dynamic obstacles must change pathing for bots and collision for players at runtime, on the server, without stalls.
Cover that stops bullets needs line-of-fire checks against new geometry, with a clear rule for which shots pass (crouched behind sandbags vs standing).
Placement validation: no building inside players, spawns, doorways or objective centres; length and curvature limits; caps per player and per team.
Damage rules per piece and weapon (splash breaks, rifles barely scratch), crushing by heavy vehicles, cutting by repair tools, ownership and cleanup.
UI: placement ghost with protected side, build progress, and readable damage states from above.
Walling off a choke, a spawn exit or an objective can stall a match; caps, no-build zones and splash that breaks walls fast keep it in check.

Fortnite-style fast building in a duel turns fights into building contests; keep building slow enough that it happens before a fight, not during it (the build-fight variant is the deliberate exception, at high spice).
Cover that is too cheap or too tough makes defence always win; cover that is too weak is never built.
From above, the height of cover is hard to read: players must see whether a piece stops shots or only movement, and which side it protects.
Wire, tank traps and sandbags need distinct silhouettes, since each stops a different kind of unit.
A changing map can confuse players; pieces must look clearly player-built (team trim, fresh look) next to the map's own walls.

variants.name: Wire obstacle
variants.summary: A coil of wire that gives no cover but stops or badly slows soldiers trying to cross it, so it funnels infantry into a kill zone; vehicles roll over it and crush it, and engineers cut it.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes Barbed Wire, Foxhole Barbed Wire, Iron Harvest barbed wire

counters.why: Soldiers can't cross the wire, so they take the long way round or walk into the defenders' kill zone.

countered_by.why: Vehicles drive over wire and crush it, opening the path for their infantry.
Engineers cut or dismantle wire quickly with their tools.

variants.name: Tank traps
variants.summary: Steel or concrete blocks that stop vehicles of both sides while soldiers walk between them; only the heaviest vehicles crush them.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes Tank Traps, Battlefield V anti-tank obstacles

counters.why: Vehicles must stop or detour around the traps, straight into the defenders' guns or mines.

countered_by.why: Soldiers pass between tank traps freely and can clear the defenders for their vehicles.
The heaviest tanks crush tank traps and drive on (Company of Heroes).
Explosives and shelling break the traps from a distance.

variants.name: Garrison bunker
variants.summary: An unarmed bunker or tower that teammates can climb into and fire out of from cover; its facing may be fixed when it is placed, and it can be captured or blown up.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest Unarmed Bunker, Red Alert 3 Soviet Combat Engineer's Battle Bunker, Tempest Rising GDF Guard Tower

adds_strengths.why: Gives teammates a hard point to fight from, protected on all sides but the firing slits.

variants.name: Fixed build spots
variants.summary: Cover can only be raised at spots the map marks, shown as outlines to builders; either side may build or use it, so the race is to finish your side's spots first.

variants.name: Energy wall
variants.summary: On a cooldown, a temporary wall of energy or ice springs up at a spot within reach and blocks movement (and shots, on some cards) for a few seconds, enough to cut off a retreat, split an enemy group or seal a gap.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Sentry's Force Field, Overwatch Mei's Ice Wall

countered_by.why: Fliers pass over a ground wall as if it were not there (StarCraft II Force Field).
The biggest units break the field by walking into it (massive units in StarCraft II).

variants.name: One-way amp wall
variants.summary: A low wall with an upper barrier that stops enemy shots from the front while the builder's team shoots out through it with a damage bonus; breaking the low base removes the whole wall.

variants.name: Build fight
variants.summary: The builder snaps walls, ramps and floors onto a grid in the middle of a fight, spending a gathered resource, to block a shot, climb above an enemy or box himself in; skill decides it, at a steep learning curve.

adds_strengths.why: Makes cover and blocks where the map has none, so its team holds ground and steers where the enemy can go.

adds_weaknesses.why: Building takes seconds in the open, the stock is small, and enemies can use or break the cover.

counters.why: Sandbags and walls stop rifle and pistol fire, so soldiers behind them win fights against small arms (Company of Heroes heavy cover).
Wire and walls close the side paths that flankers use, so they must come through the front.

countered_by.why: Explosives, mortars and shells break cover that shrugs off bullets.
Artillery hits behind cover and breaks fortified positions from far away.
Heavy vehicles and mechs drive through wire and sandbags, crushing them (Company of Heroes, Iron Harvest).
Fliers ignore ground obstacles and shoot down into a position from above.

open_questions: May enemies take cover behind your sandbags (Company of Heroes), or should cover protect only the builder's team?
Should cover go up anywhere with room (Iron Harvest, Foxhole) or only at marked spots (Battlefield V)? This draft allows anywhere outside no-build zones, with fixed spots as a variant.
Does cover stay when its builder dies or switches unit, and for how long?
Does wire hurt or only block (Company of Heroes) or slow (Foxhole) soldiers?

shooter_fit.reason: Player-built cover already works in team shooters (Battlefield V, Foxhole, Overwatch, Apex Legends) and gives builders a real job, but runtime pathing and line-of-fire changes are costly and reading cover height from above needs care.
